content.text: Writing the Theodore bar Konai page. This is the fullest single account of Mani's myth, and much of it is Mani's own words ("Mani says…").

input.content:
---
title: "Mani's myth in Theodore bar Konai"
text: true
group: scripture
order: 98
summary: The Syriac summary of Mani's teaching in Theodore bar Konai's Book of Scholia (791), much of it in Mani's own words ("Mani says…"), from the Father of Greatness and the First Man's sacrifice to the making of the world, the Messenger, the birth of Adam and Eve, and Jesus' awakening of Adam.
original_language: Syriac
source: 'Theodore bar Konai, Liber Scholiorum (791), book XI, on Mani and his teaching, as translated into French by H. Pognon, Inscriptions mandaïtes des coupes de Khouabir (Paris 1898), pp. 181–193 (archive.org `inscriptionsmand00pognuoft`) (public domain). New English translation from Pognon''s French.'
rights: "New translation © Manichaean Scripture Compendium, CC BY 4.0. Review state: draft (made from Pognon's 1898 French; not checked against the Syriac or a modern translation)."
---

## Introduction

Theodore bar Konai, a teacher of the Church of the East, finished his
*Book of Scholia* in 791. Its eleventh book is a catalogue of heresies, and
its chapter on the Manichaeans gives a hostile life of Mani and then "a
sample of the absurd teaching of the impious Manes". The sample is a string
of sentences taken from Manichaean writings, perhaps from Mani's own books,
introduced again and again with "he says" and "Mani says". It is the
fullest and most exact account of the Manichaean myth in any language
outside the Manichaean texts themselves, and it keeps the Syriac names of
the gods.

Henri Pognon published the Syriac with a French translation in 1898, in an
appendix to his edition of Mandaean bowls. He noted that the Manichaean
passage uses Mandaean words and grammar, and suggested that Mani's books
were written in an Aramaic close to Mandaic.

**This translation is a draft.** It is made from Pognon's French of 1898.
Pognon's notes on the Syriac and Mandaic words are not reproduced; where he
marked a word as uncertain, it is marked (?). The copyists left gaps, which
are marked [ … ].

## The translation

### On Mani

Many stories have been told about the impious Manes. Some have said that
he was called Kourkabios, and that he had first studied the doctrines of
the sect of the Pure, because they had bought him; that the village where he
was born was called Abroumia; that his father was called Patiq; and that
the Pure, those who are called the white-robed, being unable to bear him,
expelled him from their sect and called him "vessel of evil", which is why
he was called Manes.

Others say that he was the freedman of the wife of Bados. This Bados had
been the disciple of a certain Skountianos, who had taken up the teachings
of certain Egyptian philosophers; for he had gone to Egypt and, for that
reason, had kept company with the wise men who lived in that country at the
time, and had studied the Egyptian and Greek literatures (?), as well as the
books of Pythagoras and of Proclus (?). He is said to have brought pagan
teachings into Christianity and taught the doctrine of the two principles,
one good and the other evil, like Proclus; he gave victory to the evil
principle, and to the good desire and love. This Skountianos had as his
disciple the Bados we have spoken of; the latter, who was earlier called
Tribinthos, composed, following the doctrines he had from Skountianos, four
books, which he entitled: the first the *Book of Mysteries*, the second the
*Gospels*, the third the *Book of the Treasure*, and the fourth the *Book of
Chapters*. After writing these works he went to Babylon, where he led many
people astray. While he was performing secret magical practices, he was
struck by the spirit and died. The woman who lived with him buried him. She
took everything Bados had left, and bought a little slave about seven years
old, named Kourkabios. After freeing him, she had him taught to read and
write, and to study the books of Bados. When his mistress had died and he
had become a man, he went into the countries where Bados had taught his
doctrines, changed his name there to Manes, claimed that the four books of
Bados were his own, and took his doctrines for himself.

He used the art of medicine together with magic, and though his opinions
on everything were pagan, he wished to use the name of the Messiah so that,
by this means, he could lead many people astray. He taught people to honour
the demons as gods and to worship the sun, the moon and the stars; he also
accepted omens and the horoscope, and rejected the law of Moses, the
prophets and the God who gave the law. Of our Saviour he said that he was
born and suffered in appearance, but was not really a man as he had seemed
to be. He says that bodies come from the evil principle, denies the
resurrection, claims that one part of the world comes from God and the other
from matter, and forbids eating what has had life. All who belong to his
religion are wicked: they slaughter men in devilish mysteries, prostitute
themselves without shame, have no pity and are without hope. As for Manes,
King Sapor flayed him, filled his skin with straw, and fixed it before the
gate of Beth-Lapat, a city of the Elamites.

### On his impure teaching

We must give in this book a sample of the absurd teaching and the
blasphemous opinions of the impious Manes, to the greater shame of the
Manichaeans.

He says that before the heaven and the earth and everything in them
existed, there were two principles, the one good, the other evil. The good
one dwelt in the land of light, and he calls him the Father of Greatness.
The Manichaeans say that outside him dwell his five dwellings: intelligence,
knowledge, thought, reflection and feeling. He calls the evil principle the
King of Darkness, and says that he dwells in his dark land, in his five
worlds: the world of smoke, the world of fire, the world of wind, the world
of the waters and the world of darkness.

He adds that when the King of Darkness planned to go up to the land of
light, these five dwellings were afraid. He adds that then the Father of
Greatness reflected and said: "I will send to the war none of these five
dwellings, which are my worlds, because they were created by me for
tranquillity and peace; but I will go myself and fight against him." He
says that the Father of Greatness called forth the Mother of Life, that the
Mother of Life called forth the First Man, and that the First Man called
forth his five sons, as a man puts on his armour for battle.

He says further that an angel named Nahašbaṭ went out before him, holding in
his hand the crown of victory; that the First Man spread the light before
him; and that, on seeing him, the King of Darkness reflected and said: "What
I sought far off, I have found close at hand." Then the First Man gave
himself, with his five sons, as food to the five sons of darkness, as a man

Greatness reflected and said: "I will send to the war none of these five
dwellings, which are my worlds, because they were created by me for
tranquillity and peace; but I will go myself and fight against him." He
says that the Father of Greatness called forth the Mother of Life, that the
Mother of Life called forth the First Man, and that the First Man called
forth his five sons, as a man puts on his armour for battle.

He says further that an angel named Nahašbaṭ went out before him, holding in
his hand the crown of victory; that the First Man spread the light before
him; and that, on seeing him, the King of Darkness reflected and said: "What
I sought far off, I have found close at hand." Then the First Man gave
himself, with his five sons, as food to the five sons of darkness, as a man
who has an enemy mixes a deadly poison in a cake and gives it to him. He
adds that when the sons of darkness had eaten them, understanding was taken
from the five shining gods, and through the poison of the sons of darkness
they became like a man bitten by a mad dog or a serpent.

He adds that the First Man came to himself again and prayed seven times to
the Father of Greatness. He called forth, as the second creation, the Friend
of the Lights; the Friend of the Lights called forth the Great Ban (the
Builder); the Great Ban called forth the Living Spirit; and the Living Spirit
called forth his five sons: the Ornament of Splendour from his intelligence,
the Great King of Honour from his knowledge, Adamas-Light from his reason,
the King of Glory from his thought, and the Bearer from his reflection.

They went to the land of darkness and found the First Man swallowed up by
the darkness, he and his five sons. Then the Living Spirit spoke a word,
and the word of the Living Spirit took the form of a sharp sword. He made the
image of the First Man appear and said to him: "Greetings to you, good one
among the wicked, shining one in the midst of darkness, god who dwells among
the beasts of wrath who do not know their honour!" The First Man answered
him: "Come in the peace of the dead (?); come, treasure (?) of calm and
peace!" He said further: "How are our fathers, the sons of light, in their
city?" The Caller answered him: "They are well." The Living Spirit, the
Caller and the Answerer came together and went up to the Mother of Life and
the Living Spirit. The Living Spirit put on the Caller, and the Mother of
Life put on the Answerer, her beloved son. They went down to the land of
darkness, to the place where the First Man and his sons were.

Then the Spirit commanded three of his sons that one should kill and
another flay the archons, the sons of darkness, and that they should bring
them to the Mother of Life. The Mother of Life stretched out the heaven from
their skins; she made eleven heavens, and they threw their bodies down on the
land of darkness. They made eight earths, and the five sons of the Living
Spirit each received a task (?). It was the Ornament of Splendour who held
the five shining gods by their loins, and below their loins the heavens
were spread out. It was the Bearer who, kneeling on one knee, bore the
earths. When the heavens and the earths had been made, the Great King of
Honour sat in the midst of the heaven and kept watch to guard them all.

Then the Living Spirit revealed his forms to the sons of darkness; he
purified some of the light they had swallowed, taking it from those five
shining gods, and made the sun, the moon, and more than a thousand lights.
She made the vessels: wind, water and fire. He went down and formed them
below, near the Bearer. The King of Glory called forth and set over them
wheels (?), so that they might rise over those archons cast down on the
earths, to serve the five shining gods, lest they be burned by the poison of
the archons [ … ].

Mani says that the Mother of Life, the First Man and the Living Spirit
began to pray and beseech the Father of Greatness. The Father of Greatness
heard them and called forth, as the third creation, the Messenger. The
Messenger called forth the twelve virgins with their robes, their crowns and
their attributes: the first was Royalty, the second Wisdom, the third
Victory, the fourth Persuasion, the fifth Purity, the sixth Truth, the
seventh Faith, the eighth Patience, the ninth Equity, the tenth Goodness, the
eleventh Uprightness, the twelfth Light. When the Messenger came to these
ships [ … ], he charged three servants to make them move; he charged the
Great Ban to build a new earth, and the three vessels (wheels?) to rise.

When the ships moved and reached the middle of the heaven, the Messenger
showed his forms, both the male form and the female form, and he was seen
by all the archons, the sons of darkness, male and female. At the sight of
the Messenger, who was beautiful in his forms, all the archons were filled
with desire: the males desired the female form and the females the male
form, and in their desire they began to give up the light they had
swallowed, taking it from the five shining gods. Then the sin that had been
imprisoned (?) in them mixed with the light that came out of the archons,
in the proportion in which it had been swallowed. They wanted to enter in,
but the Messenger hid his forms, and cut off the light of the five shining
gods, and the sin that was with them.

The sin that came out of the archons fell back on them, but they did not
take it back, like a man who loathes his own spittle. Then this sin fell
on the earth, half on the wet part and half on the dry. (On the wet part)
it turned into a horrible beast, like the King of Darkness. Adamas-Light
was sent against it, gave it battle and overcame it. He threw it on its
back, struck it in the aorta of its heart, thrust his shield over its
mouth, and set one foot on its thighs and the other on its breast. The sin
that had fallen on the dry part began to sprout in the form of five trees.

Mani says that those daughters of darkness were pregnant before, of their
own nature. Because of the beauty of the Messenger's forms, which they had
seen, they miscarried; their unborn young fell on the earth and ate the
buds of the trees. The abortions took counsel among themselves and
remembered the form of the Messenger they had seen. They said: "Where is the
form we saw?" Ašaqlūn, son of the King of Darkness, said to the abortions:
"Give me your sons and your daughters, and I will make you a form like the
one you saw." They brought them and gave them to him; but he ate the males
and gave the females to Namraēl, his companion. Namraēl and Ašaqlūn came
together; Namraēl conceived and bore to Ašaqlūn a son, whom she named Adam;
she conceived and bore a daughter, whom she named Eve.

Mani says further that Jesus the Splendour drew near to the senseless Adam
and woke him from a sleep of death, so that he might be freed from many
spirits (?). As a righteous man who finds a man possessed by a fearsome
demon and calms him by his art, so it was with Adam, since that friend
found him sunk in a deep sleep, woke him, made him move, drew him out of
sleep, drove the seducing demon from him, and bound far from him the great
troop of the archons.

Then Adam examined himself and knew who he was. Jesus showed him the
Fathers who dwell on high, and his own self, exposed to everything, to the
teeth of the panther, to the teeth of the elephant, swallowed by the
voracious, gulped down by those who gulp (?), eaten by the dogs, mixed and
imprisoned in all that exists, bound in the stench of darkness. Mani adds
that he made him stand up and taste of the Tree of Life. Then Adam looked
and wept. He raised his voice loud like a roaring lion, tore his hair, cried
out (?), beat his breast and said: "Woe, woe to the maker of my body, to the
one who bound my soul, and to the rebels who have enslaved me!"

## Notes to this edition

- **The life of Mani** in Theodore's first section is the hostile Christian
  legend first told in the *Acta Archelai* (the slave Kourkabios inheriting
  the books of Terebinthus-"Bados" and Scythianus); it is given here because
  it is part of the same chapter, but it is not Manichaean.
- **The gods** have their Syriac names: the Father of Greatness, the Mother
  of Life, the First Man; the Friend of the Lights, the Great Ban (the
  Builder), the Living Spirit; the Messenger (the Third Envoy). The five
  sons of the Living Spirit are the Ornament of Splendour (Splenditenens),
  the Great King of Honour, Adamas-Light, the King of Glory and the Bearer
  (Omophoros). Compare the same gods in Middle Persian and Turkish in [the
  Šābuhragān](shabuhragan.html), [the building of the
  world](turfan-cosmogony.html) and [Old Turkish texts from
  Qočo](turkish-manichaica-1.html).
- **The Caller and the Answerer** (Xrōštag and Padvāxtag in the Iranian
  texts) appear in the Chinese [Traité](traite.html) and Hymnscroll too.
- **Gaps.** Pognon noted that the copyists left out at least one passage
  before "these ships" (the making of the sun and moon as ships) and that a
  passage on the vessels is confused.

---
title: "Mani's letter to Marcellus, and Turbo's account of his teaching (Acta Archelai)"
text: true
group: extracanonical
order: 90
summary: The letter of "Manichaeus, apostle of Jesus Christ" to Marcellus, and the disciple Turbo's report of Mani's teaching (the two kingdoms, the First Man, the Living Spirit, the wheel and the ships of light, the Maiden and the archons), from the Acts of Archelaus.
original_language: Greek (lost) and Latin
source: 'Hegemonius, Acta Archelai (4th century), chapters 5 and 7–9, in the edition of C. H. Beeson, Die griechischen christlichen Schriftsteller 16 (Leipzig 1906), pp. 5–15 (archive.org `actaarchelaihrsg00hegeuoft`). New translation from the Latin, compared with the Greek preserved by Epiphanius.'
rights: "New translation © Manichaean Scripture Compendium, CC BY 4.0. Review state: draft (made from Beeson's Latin, read from an OCR scan; not checked against another translation)."
---

## Introduction

The *Acts of Archelaus* is a fourth-century Christian work, written in Greek
by one Hegemonius and surviving whole only in Latin. It tells how Mani
wrote to a rich Christian, Marcellus, of the city of Carchar in Roman
Mesopotamia, and came to debate with its bishop, Archelaus. The story is
fiction, but the work preserves two Manichaean pieces. The first is a letter
that opens "Manichaeus, apostle of Jesus Christ", the formula Mani used at
the head of his letters, and is presented as Mani's own. The second is the
report of Mani's former disciple Turbo, who sets out "the faith of Mani"
point by point; its contents agree closely with the Manichaean texts found
since. Epiphanius copied both into his *Panarion* in the original Greek,
so the Latin can be checked against it.

The *Acts* are not on Wikipedia's list of Manichaean texts that this
compendium follows, so this page is filed as related material.

**This translation is new and is a draft.** It is made from the Latin of
Beeson's edition (1906), read from an OCR scan, with the Greek of
Epiphanius printed beside it consulted where the Latin is unclear. Words in
parentheses are added for sense.

## The translation

### The letter to Marcellus (chapter 5)

Manichaeus, apostle of Jesus Christ, and all the saints and virgins who are
with me, to Marcellus, my dearest son: grace, mercy and peace from God the
Father and our Lord Jesus Christ; and may the right hand of light keep you
from this present evil age, and from its ruins and the snares of the evil
one. Amen.

Feeling your boundless love, I rejoiced greatly; but that your faith is not
according to right reason grieved me. So, since I have been sent to set
right the human race, and to help those who have given themselves up to
seductions and errors, I have thought it necessary to send you this
writing: first for the salvation of your own soul, and then of those who
are with you, so that you may not have a mind that makes no distinctions,
as the teachers of the simpler folk teach, saying that evil and good come
from the same author, and bringing in a single beginning, and not
examining or distinguishing the darkness from the light, or the good from
the evil, or the outer man from the inner, as we said before, but never
ceasing to confuse and mix the one with the other.

But you, my son, do not, like most men, mix both together without reason,
simply and without distinction, and do not insult the God of goodness. For
they refer the beginning and the end, and the father of these evils, to
God, whose end is close to a curse. For they do not believe what is said in
the Gospels of our Saviour and Lord Jesus Christ, that a bad tree cannot
bear good fruit, nor a good tree bad fruit. How they dare to call God the
maker and creator of Satan and of his evil deeds, I greatly wonder. And
would that their folly had gone no further than this, and that they did
not say that the only-begotten Christ, who came down from the bosom of the
Father, was the son of a certain woman, Mary, begotten of blood and flesh
and the other filth of women!

And so as not to write much in this letter and draw out your patience at
length, since I have no natural eloquence, it is enough to have said this.
You will learn everything when I am with you, if indeed you are eager to
spare and look after your salvation; for I cast a noose on no one, as most
of the foolish do. Understand what I say, honoured son.

### Turbo's account of Mani's teaching (chapters 7–9)

*Archelaus asks Turbo, who has come from Mani with the letter, to tell what
Mani teaches. Turbo begins: Mani worships two gods, unbegotten, self-made
and eternal, the one opposed to the other; the one is good, the other evil;
the one is called Light, the other Darkness … (the opening of his account is
given here only in summary). He goes on:*

[It is] as if two kings were fighting each other, who had been enemies
from the beginning, each having his own portion; and it happened that the
darkness went forth from its bounds and joined battle with the light.

When the good Father learned that the darkness had come upon his land, he
brought forth from himself a power, which is called the Mother of Life,
and with it he surrounded the First Man; these are the five elements, that
is, wind, light, water, fire and matter. Clothed with these, as if with the
equipment of war, he went down to fight against the darkness. But the
princes of the darkness, fighting against him, ate of his armour, which is
the soul. Then the First Man, our first parent, was grievously afflicted
down there by the darkness; and had not the Father heard him as he prayed,
and sent another power which had gone forth from himself, which is called
the Living Spirit, and had it not come down and given him its right hand
and led him out of the darkness, the First Man would long ago have been held
fast and in peril. So he left the soul down there. And this is why the
Manichaeans, when they meet one another, give each other the right hand, as
a sign of this, as men set free from the darkness; for all heresy, he says,
is in darkness.

Then the Living Spirit made the world; and clothed with three other powers,
he went down, brought up the princes and crucified them in the firmament,
which is their body, the sphere. And again the Living Spirit himself made
the lights, which are the remains of the soul, and made them go round the
firmament; and again he made the earth, and there are eight (earths). And
the Omophoros is below, that is, the one who carries it on his shoulders;
and when he grows tired of carrying, he trembles, and this is the cause of
earthquakes out of their appointed time. For this reason the good Father
sent his son from his bosom into the heart of the earth and its inner

-## Introduction
-The *Acts of Archelaus* is a fourth-century Christian work, written in Greek
-by one Hegemonius and surviving whole only in Latin. It tells how Mani
-wrote to a rich Christian, Marcellus, of the city of Carchar in Roman
-Mesopotamia, and came to debate with its bishop, Archelaus. The story is
-fiction, but the work preserves two Manichaean pieces. The first is a letter
-that opens "Manichaeus, apostle of Jesus Christ", the formula Mani used at
-the head of his letters, and is presented as Mani's own. The second is the
-report of Mani's former disciple Turbo, who sets out "the faith of Mani"
-point by point; its contents agree closely with the Manichaean texts found
-since. Epiphanius copied both into his *Panarion* in the original Greek,
-so the Latin can be checked against it.
-The *Acts* are not on Wikipedia's list of Manichaean texts that this
-compendium follows, so this page is filed as related material.
-**This translation is new and is a draft.** It is made from the Latin of
-Beeson's edition (1906), read from an OCR scan, with the Greek of
-Epiphanius printed beside it consulted where the Latin is unclear. Words in
-parentheses are added for sense.
-## The translation
-### The letter to Marcellus (chapter 5)
-Manichaeus, apostle of Jesus Christ, and all the saints and virgins who are
-with me, to Marcellus, my dearest son: grace, mercy and peace from God the
-Father and our Lord Jesus Christ; and may the right hand of light keep you
-from this present evil age, and from its ruins and the snares of the evil
-one. Amen.
-Feeling your boundless love, I rejoiced greatly; but that your faith is not
-according to right reason grieved me. So, since I have been sent to set
-right the human race, and to help those who have given themselves up to
-seductions and errors, I have thought it necessary to send you this
-writing: first for the salvation of your own soul, and then of those who
-are with you, so that you may not have a mind that makes no distinctions,
-as the teachers of the simpler folk teach, saying that evil and good come
-from the same author, and bringing in a single beginning, and not
-examining or distinguishing the darkness from the light, or the good from
-the evil, or the outer man from the inner, as we said before, but never
-ceasing to confuse and mix the one with the other.
-But you, my son, do not, like most men, mix both together without reason,
-simply and without distinction, and do not insult the God of goodness. For
-they refer the beginning and the end, and the father of these evils, to
-God, whose end is close to a curse. For they do not believe what is said in
-the Gospels of our Saviour and Lord Jesus Christ, that a bad tree cannot
-bear good fruit, nor a good tree bad fruit. How they dare to call God the
-maker and creator of Satan and of his evil deeds, I greatly wonder. And
-would that their folly had gone no further than this, and that they did
-not say that the only-begotten Christ, who came down from the bosom of the
-Father, was the son of a certain woman, Mary, begotten of blood and flesh
-and the other filth of women!
-And so as not to write much in this letter and draw out your patience at
-length, since I have no natural eloquence, it is enough to have said this.
-You will learn everything when I am with you, if indeed you are eager to
-spare and look after your salvation; for I cast a noose on no one, as most
-of the foolish do. Understand what I say, honoured son.
-### Turbo's account of Mani's teaching (chapters 7–9)
-*Archelaus asks Turbo, who has come from Mani with the letter, to tell what
-Mani teaches. Turbo begins: Mani worships two gods, unbegotten, self-made
-and eternal, the one opposed to the other; the one is good, the other evil;
-the one is called Light, the other Darkness … (the opening of his account is
-given here only in summary). He goes on:*
-[It is] as if two kings were fighting each other, who had been enemies
-from the beginning, each having his own portion; and it happened that the
-darkness went forth from its bounds and joined battle with the light.
-When the good Father learned that the darkness had come upon his land, he
-brought forth from himself a power, which is called the Mother of Life,
-and with it he surrounded the First Man; these are the five elements, that
-is, wind, light, water, fire and matter. Clothed with these, as if with the
-equipment of war, he went down to fight against the darkness. But the
-princes of the darkness, fighting against him, ate of his armour, which is
-the soul. Then the First Man, our first parent, was grievously afflicted
-down there by the darkness; and had not the Father heard him as he prayed,
-and sent another power which had gone forth from himself, which is called
-the Living Spirit, and had it not come down and given him its right hand
-and led him out of the darkness, the First Man would long ago have been held
-fast and in peril. So he left the soul down there. And this is why the
-Manichaeans, when they meet one another, give each other the right hand, as
-a sign of this, as men set free from the darkness; for all heresy, he says,
-is in darkness.
-Then the Living Spirit made the world; and clothed with three other powers,
-he went down, brought up the princes and crucified them in the firmament,
-which is their body, the sphere. And again the Living Spirit himself made
-the lights, which are the remains of the soul, and made them go round the
-firmament; and again he made the earth, and there are eight (earths). And
-the Omophoros is below, that is, the one who carries it on his shoulders;
-and when he grows tired of carrying, he trembles, and this is the cause of
-earthquakes out of their appointed time. For this reason the good Father
-sent his son from his bosom into the heart of the earth and its inner
-parts, to restrain him as was fitting; for whenever there is an earthquake,
-it is caused by his trembling from fatigue, or by his shifting the weight
-from one shoulder to the other.
-Then Matter too made plants (or shoots) out of itself; and when these were
-stolen by certain princes, it called together all the chief princes, took
-from each of them a single power, and made this man after the likeness of
-that First Man, and bound the soul in him. This is the basis of the mixture.
-When the living Father saw the soul afflicted in the body, because he is
-compassionate and merciful, he sent his beloved son for the salvation of the
-soul; for this reason, and because of the Omophoros, he sent him. And the
-son came and changed himself into the likeness of a man; he appeared to men
-as a man, though he was not a man, and men thought he had been born.
-When he had come, he set up a device put together for the salvation of
-souls, that is, a wheel, with twelve buckets, which turns with this sphere
-and draws up the souls of the dying; and the greater light, that is, the
-sun, takes them with its rays, purifies them and hands them to the moon, and
-so the disc of the moon, as we call it, is filled. For he says that these
-two lights are ships or ferry-boats; and when the moon is full, it ferries
-the souls across to the eastern region, and so makes its waning, when it is
-relieved of its load; and the boats are filled again and unloaded again,
-while the souls are drawn up by the buckets, until it has set free its own
-part of the souls. He holds that every soul, and every living thing that
-moves, takes its part from the substance of the good Father. So when the
-moon has handed over the load of souls it carries to the aeons of the
-Father, they remain in the Column of Glory, which is called the Perfect
-Man. This Man is a column of light, for it is filled with pure souls; and
-this is the cause of the salvation of souls.
-The cause of death for men is this. A certain Maiden, fair and adorned and
-very graceful, by stealth draws on the princes who are in the firmament,
-who were brought up and crucified by the Living Spirit. When she appears,
-to the males she appears as a fair woman, to the females she shows herself
-as a handsome and desirable young man. And the princes, when they see her
-adorned, are moved to lust by love of her; and because they cannot seize
-her, they are violently driven on, kindled by the fires of love, for they
-are carried away by the heat of desire. So when, as they run after her, the
-maiden suddenly vanishes, then that great prince brings forth clouds from
-himself, to darken the whole world in his anger; and when he has been
-greatly troubled, as a man sweats after toil, so this prince too sweats from
-his trouble, and his sweat is the rain. And the prince of the harvest (of
-pestilence), too, if he has been deceived by the maiden, pours out famine
-(plague) over the whole earth, so as to bring death on men. For this body is
-called a world, after the likeness of this great world; and all men who are
-below have their roots bound to those above. So when (that prince) has been
-deceived by the maiden, then he begins to cut the roots of men; and when
-their roots are cut, then pestilence begins, and so they die. And if he
-shakes the upper parts of the root, an earthquake comes and follows, as the
-Omophoros is shaken too. This is the cause of death.
-## Notes to this edition
-- **The opening of the letter** follows the form of Paul's letters, as
-  Mani's letters did; the Turfan Middle Persian Gospel fragment has the same
-  self-description, "I, Mani, the apostle of Jesus the Friend" ([Mani's
-  Gospel and Epistles](turfan-gospel-epistles.html)).
-- **"The right hand of light"**: the giving of the right hand among
-  Manichaeans, explained by Turbo as a memory of the Living Spirit giving
-  his right hand to the First Man, is found in the Coptic and Iranian texts
-  too.
-- **"The prince of the harvest"**: the Latin translator read the Greek
-  *limos* ("famine") where Epiphanius has *loimos* ("plague"), so the Latin
-  has "famine"; both are given.
-- **Turbo's account goes on** (chapters 10–13) to the transmigration of
-  souls, the rules for the Elect and the hearers, the prayers, and the end
-  of the world; those chapters are not yet translated here.
-- **The wheel with twelve buckets, the ships of light, the Column of Glory
-  and the seducing Maiden** are the same images as in the Coptic, Iranian
-  and Chinese texts; compare [Theodore bar Konai](theodore-bar-konai.html)
-  and the [Turfan cosmogony](turfan-cosmogony.html).

+Feeling your boundless love, I rejoiced greatly; but that your faith is not
+according to right reason grieved me. So, since I have been sent to set
+right the human race, and to help those who have given themselves up to
+seductions and errors, I have thought it necessary to send you this
+writing: first for the salvation of your own soul, and then of those who
+are with you, so that you may not have a mind that makes no distinctions,
+as the teachers of the simpler folk teach, saying that evil and good come
+from the same author, and bringing in a single beginning, and not
+examining or distinguishing the darkness from the light, or the good from
+the evil, or the outer man from the inner, as we said before, but never
+ceasing to confuse and mix the one with the other.
+But you, my son, do not, like most men, mix both together without reason,
+simply and without distinction, and do not insult the God of goodness. For
+they refer the beginning and the end, and the father of these evils, to
+God, whose end is close to a curse. For they do not believe what is said in
+the Gospels of our Saviour and Lord Jesus Christ, that a bad tree cannot
+bear good fruit, nor a good tree bad fruit. How they dare to call God the
+maker and creator of Satan and of his evil deeds, I greatly wonder. And
+would that their folly had gone no further than this, and that they did
+not say that the only-begotten Christ, who came down from the bosom of the
+Father, was the son of a certain woman, Mary, begotten of blood and flesh
+and the other filth of women!
+And so as not to write much in this letter and draw out your patience at
+length, since I have no natural eloquence, it is enough to have said this.
+You will learn everything when I am with you, if indeed you are eager to
+spare and look after your salvation; for I cast a noose on no one, as most
+of the foolish do. Understand what I say, honoured son.
+### Turbo's account of Mani's teaching (chapters 7–9)
+*Archelaus and Marcellus ask Turbo, who has brought the letter from Mani,
+to tell what Mani teaches. Turbo answers:*
+If you wish to learn from me the faith of Mani, hear it briefly. He
+worships two gods, unbegotten, existing of themselves, eternal, the one
+opposed to the other; and he brings in the one as good and the other as
+evil. To the one he gives the name Light, and to the other Darkness. And
+(he says) that the soul which is in men is part of the light, and the body,
+and the creation that comes from matter, of the darkness. He says that the
+mixture or union came about in this way, likening the two gods to an
+example of this kind:
+[It is] as if two kings were fighting each other, who had been enemies
+from the beginning, each having his own portion; and it happened that the
+darkness went forth from its bounds and joined battle with the light.
+When the good Father learned that the darkness had come upon his land, he
+brought forth from himself a power, which is called the Mother of Life,
+and with it he surrounded the First Man; these are the five elements, that
+is, wind, light, water, fire and matter. Clothed with these, as if with the
+equipment of war, he went down to fight against the darkness. But the
+princes of the darkness, fighting against him, ate of his armour, which is
+the soul. Then the First Man, our first parent, was grievously afflicted
+down there by the darkness; and had not the Father heard him as he prayed,
+and sent another power which had gone forth from himself, which is called
+the Living Spirit, and had it not come down and given him its right hand
+and led him out of the darkness, the First Man would long ago have been held
+fast and in peril. So he left the soul down there. And this is why the
+Manichaeans, when they meet one another, give each other the right hand, as
+a sign of this, as men set free from the darkness; for all heresy, he says,
+is in darkness.
+Then the Living Spirit made the world; and clothed with three other powers,
+he went down, brought up the princes and crucified them in the firmament,
+which is their body, the sphere. And again the Living Spirit himself made
+the lights, which are the remains of the soul, and made them go round the
+firmament; and again he made the earth, and there are eight (earths). And
+the Omophoros is below, that is, the one who carries it on his shoulders;
+and when he grows tired of carrying, he trembles, and this is the cause of
+earthquakes out of their appointed time. For this reason the good Father
+sent his son from his bosom into the heart of the earth and its inner
+parts, to restrain him as was fitting; for whenever there is an earthquake,
+it is caused by his trembling from fatigue, or by his shifting the weight
+from one shoulder to the other.
+Then Matter too made plants (or shoots) out of itself; and when these were
+stolen by certain princes, it called together all the chief princes, took
+from each of them a single power, and made this man after the likeness of
+that First Man, and bound the soul in him. This is the basis of the mixture.
+When the living Father saw the soul afflicted in the body, because he is
+compassionate and merciful, he sent his beloved son for the salvation of the
+soul; for this reason, and because of the Omophoros, he sent him. And the
+son came and changed himself into the likeness of a man; he appeared to men
+as a man, though he was not a man, and men thought he had been born.
+When he had come, he set up a device put together for the salvation of
+souls, that is, a wheel, with twelve buckets, which turns with this sphere
+and draws up the souls of the dying; and the greater light, that is, the
+sun, takes them with its rays, purifies them and hands them to the moon, and
+so the disc of the moon, as we call it, is filled. For he says that these
+two lights are ships or ferry-boats; and when the moon is full, it ferries
+the souls across to the eastern region, and so makes its waning, when it is
+relieved of its load; and the boats are filled again and unloaded again,
+while the souls are drawn up by the buckets, until it has set free its own
+part of the souls. He holds that every soul, and every living thing that
+moves, takes its part from the substance of the good Father. So when the
+moon has handed over the load of souls it carries to the aeons of the
+Father, they remain in the Column of Glory, which is called the Perfect
+Man. This Man is a column of light, for it is filled with pure souls; and
+this is the cause of the salvation of souls.
+The cause of death for men is this. A certain Maiden, fair and adorned and
+very graceful, by stealth draws on the princes who are in the firmament,
+who were brought up and crucified by the Living Spirit. When she appears,
+to the males she appears as a fair woman, to the females she shows herself
+as a handsome and desirable young man. And the princes, when they see her
+adorned, are moved to lust by love of her; and because they cannot seize
+her, they are violently driven on, kindled by the fires of love, for they
+are carried away by the heat of desire. So when, as they run after her, the
+maiden suddenly vanishes, then that great prince brings forth clouds from
+himself, to darken the whole world in his anger; and when he has been
+greatly troubled, as a man sweats after toil, so this prince too sweats from
+his trouble, and his sweat is the rain. And the prince of the harvest (of
+pestilence), too, if he has been deceived by the maiden, pours out famine
+(plague) over the whole earth, so as to bring death on men. For this body is
+called a world, after the likeness of this great world; and all men who are
+below have their roots bound to those above. So when (that prince) has been
+deceived by the maiden, then he begins to cut the roots of men; and when
+their roots are cut, then pestilence begins, and so they die. And if he
+shakes the upper parts of the root, an earthquake comes and follows, as the
+Omophoros is shaken too. This is the cause of death.
+## Notes to this edition
+- **The opening of the letter** follows the form of Paul's letters, as
+  Mani's letters did; the Turfan Middle Persian Gospel fragment has the same
+  self-description, "I, Mani, the apostle of Jesus the Friend" ([Mani's
+  Gospel and Epistles](turfan-gospel-epistles.html)).
+- **"The right hand of light"**: the giving of the right hand among
+  Manichaeans, explained by Turbo as a memory of the Living Spirit giving
+  his right hand to the First Man, is found in the Coptic and Iranian texts
+  too.
+- **"The prince of the harvest"**: the Latin translator read the Greek
+  *limos* ("famine") where Epiphanius has *loimos* ("plague"), so the Latin
+  has "famine"; both are given.
+- **Turbo's account goes on** (chapters 10–13) to the transmigration of
+  souls, the rules for the Elect and the hearers, the prayers, and the end
+  of the world; those chapters are not yet translated here.
+- **The wheel with twelve buckets, the ships of light, the Column of Glory
+  and the seducing Maiden** are the same images as in the Coptic, Iranian
+  and Chinese texts; compare [Theodore bar Konai](theodore-bar-konai.html)
+  and the [Turfan cosmogony](turfan-cosmogony.html).

### Turbo's account, continued (chapters 10–13)

*(Chapter 10 begins:) "I will tell you this too, how the soul is poured over
into five bodies."*

First a little of it is purified in this one; then it is poured over into
a dog, or a camel, or the body of another animal. If it has committed
murder, the soul is poured over into the bodies of lepers; if it has cut the
harvest, into the dumb. The names of the soul are these: mind, sense,
prudence, understanding, thought.

The reapers who reap the harvest are likened to the princes who, sprung
from matter, have been in the darkness since they ate of the armour of the
First Man; that is why they must be poured over into hay, or beans, or
barley, or ears of corn, or vegetables, so that they too may be cut and
mown. And whoever eats bread must himself be eaten, having become bread.
Whoever kills a chicken will himself be a chicken; whoever kills a mouse
will himself be a mouse. If anyone is rich in this world, when he leaves
his body he must be thrown into the body of a poor man, so that he walks
about and begs, and after that he goes to eternal punishment. Since this
body belongs to the princes and to matter, whoever plants a persea tree
must pass through many bodies, until that persea he planted falls. Whoever
builds himself a house will be scattered through all bodies. If anyone
washes himself in water, he wounds his soul; and whoever does not give food
to his (Mani's) Elect will be subjected to the punishments of hell and be
changed into the bodies of hearers, until he does many works of mercy. For
this reason, whatever is best among foods they offer to those Elect.

And when they want to eat bread, they first pray, saying this to the bread:
"I did not reap you, nor grind you, nor knead you, nor put you in the oven;
another made you and brought you to me; I eat you without guilt." And when
he has said this to himself, he answers the one who brought it: "I have
prayed for you"; and so that one goes away. For, as I told you a little
before, if anyone reaps, he will be reaped; so too, if anyone puts corn into
the mill, he will himself be put into the mill; or if he kneads, he will be
kneaded; or if he bakes bread, he will be baked; and for this reason it is
forbidden among them to do work.

And again they say that there are other worlds besides this one we see, on
which the lights of this world rise when they set here. And they say that
if anyone walks on the earth, he hurts the earth; and whoever moves his hand
hurts the air, because the air is the soul of men and animals and birds and
fishes and creeping things and whatever is in this world. For I told you
that this body is not of God, but is of matter and of darkness, and so it
must be darkened.

*(Chapter 11.)* The so-called Paradise is the world. The trees in it are
the desires and the other seductions that corrupt men's thoughts. But that
tree in Paradise from which the good is known is Jesus himself, and his
knowledge, which is in the world; whoever receives it distinguishes good
from evil. The world itself is not God's either, but was formed out of a
part of matter, and so all things are destroyed. What the princes stole
from the First Man is what fills the moon, what is purified every day from
the world. And if a soul goes out that has not known the truth, it is
handed over to the demons, to be tamed in the hell of fire; and after it has
been chastised, it is poured over into other bodies, to be tamed, and so it
is thrown into that great fire until the end.

Of the prophets who are among you he says this: that they are spirits of
the impiety, or lawlessness, of that darkness which rose up in the
beginning; deceived by it, they did not speak in truth; for that prince
blinded their mind. And if anyone follows their words, he will die for
ever, bound in the mass, because he has not learned the knowledge of the
Paraclete.

He commanded his Elect alone, who are no more than seven in number, that
when they have finished eating they should pray, and put on their heads oil
over which spells have been spoken, calling on many names, to strengthen
this faith; but he did not reveal the names to me, for only those seven use
these names. And again, the name Sabaoth, which is great and honoured among
you, he says is the nature of man and the father of desire; and that is
why, he says, the simpler people worship desire, thinking it a god.

*(Chapter 12.)* Of how Adam was made, he says this: that the one who said,
"Come, let us make man in our image and likeness", and after the form we
have seen, is the prince, who says this to the princes his colleagues:
"Come, give me of the light we have received, and let us make (man) after
our form, we who are princes, and after the form we have seen, which is the
First Man"; and so they made man. They made Eve likewise, giving her of
their desire to deceive Adam; and through these things the fashioning of
the world came about by the creation of the prince.

(He says) that God has no part with the world and does not rejoice over it,
because from the beginning he was robbed by the princes and trouble arose
for him. For this reason he sends and steals from them his soul every day
through these lights, that is, the sun and the moon, by which the whole
world and all creation are carried off. The one who spoke with Moses and
the Jews and the priests he says is the prince of darkness; and so the
Christians, the Jews and the pagans are one and the same, worshipping the
same god; for he deceives them in his desires, since he is not the god of
truth. Therefore all who hope in that god who spoke with Moses and the
prophets must be handed over to chains with him, because they did not hope
in the God of truth; for that one spoke with them according to his own
desires.

*(Chapter 13.)* After all this, at the last, he says, as the Elder himself
wrote: when he has made his image manifest, then the Omophoros himself lets
the earth go from him, and so that great fire is let loose which consumes
the whole world; then again they let down the mass (Greek *bōlos*), which
is thrown into the midst of the new age, so that all the souls of the
sinners may be bound for ever. These things will happen when the Statue
comes.

All the emanations are: Jesus in the small ship, and the Mother of Life,
and the twelve helmsmen, and the Maiden of Light, and the third Elder.
Hence the Living Spirit, too, is set in the larger ship, and the wall of
that great fire, and the wall of wind and of air and of water and of the
inner living fire, all of which dwell in the moon (the small light), until
the fire consumes the whole world; in how many years, I have not learned.
And after this there will be the restoration of the two natures: the
princes will dwell in their lower parts, and the Father in the higher,
receiving back what is his own.

This is all the teaching that he handed on to his three disciples, and he
told them to set out for the three regions of the world. Of these, Adda was
allotted the parts of the East, Thomas received the lands of the Syrians,
and Hermas set out for Egypt; and to this day they live there, for the sake
of preaching this doctrine.

### Turbo's account, continued (chapters 10–13)

*(Chapter 10 begins:) "I will tell you this too, how the soul is poured over
into five bodies."*

First a little of it is purified in this one; then it is poured over into
a dog, or a camel, or the body of another animal. If it has committed
murder, the soul is poured over into the bodies of lepers; if it has cut the
harvest, into the dumb. The names of the soul are these: mind, sense,
prudence, understanding, thought.

The reapers who reap the harvest are likened to the princes who, sprung
from matter, have been in the darkness since they ate of the armour of the
First Man; that is why they must be poured over into hay, or beans, or
barley, or ears of corn, or vegetables, so that they too may be cut and
mown. And whoever eats bread must himself be eaten, having become bread.
Whoever kills a chicken will himself be a chicken; whoever kills a mouse
will himself be a mouse. If anyone is rich in this world, when he leaves
his body he must be thrown into the body of a poor man, so that he walks
about and begs, and after that he goes to eternal punishment. Since this
body belongs to the princes and to matter, whoever plants a persea tree
must pass through many bodies, until that persea he planted falls. Whoever
builds himself a house will be scattered through all bodies. If anyone
washes himself in water, he wounds his soul; and whoever does not give food
to his (Mani's) Elect will be subjected to the punishments of hell and be
changed into the bodies of hearers, until he does many works of mercy. For
this reason, whatever is best among foods they offer to those Elect.

And when they want to eat bread, they first pray, saying this to the bread:
"I did not reap you, nor grind you, nor knead you, nor put you in the oven;
another made you and brought you to me; I eat you without guilt." And when
he has said this to himself, he answers the one who brought it: "I have
prayed for you"; and so that one goes away. For, as I told you a little
before, if anyone reaps, he will be reaped; so too, if anyone puts corn into
the mill, he will himself be put into the mill; or if he kneads, he will be
kneaded; or if he bakes bread, he will be baked; and for this reason it is
forbidden among them to do work.

And again they say that there are other worlds besides this one we see, on
which the lights of this world rise when they set here. And they say that
if anyone walks on the earth, he hurts the earth; and whoever moves his hand
hurts the air, because the air is the soul of men and animals and birds and
fishes and creeping things and whatever is in this world. For I told you
that this body is not of God, but is of matter and of darkness, and so it
must be darkened.

*(Chapter 11.)* The so-called Paradise is the world. The trees in it are
the desires and the other seductions that corrupt men's thoughts. But that
tree in Paradise from which the good is known is Jesus himself, and his
knowledge, which is in the world; whoever receives it distinguishes good
from evil. The world itself is not God's either, but was formed out of a
part of matter, and so all things are destroyed. What the princes stole
from the First Man is what fills the moon, what is purified every day from
the world. And if a soul goes out that has not known the truth, it is
handed over to the demons, to be tamed in the hell of fire; and after it has
been chastised, it is poured over into other bodies, to be tamed, and so it
is thrown into that great fire until the end.

Of the prophets who are among you he says this: that they are spirits of
the impiety, or lawlessness, of that darkness which rose up in the
beginning; deceived by it, they did not speak in truth; for that prince
blinded their mind. And if anyone follows their words, he will die for
ever, bound in the mass, because he has not learned the knowledge of the
Paraclete.

He commanded his Elect alone, who are no more than seven in number, that
when they have finished eating they should pray, and put on their heads oil
over which spells have been spoken, calling on many names, to strengthen
this faith; but he did not reveal the names to me, for only those seven use
these names. And again, the name Sabaoth, which is great and honoured among
you, he says is the nature of man and the father of desire; and that is
why, he says, the simpler people worship desire, thinking it a god.

*(Chapter 12.)* Of how Adam was made, he says this: that the one who said,
"Come, let us make man in our image and likeness", and after the form we
have seen, is the prince, who says this to the princes his colleagues:
"Come, give me of the light we have received, and let us make (man) after
our form, we who are princes, and after the form we have seen, which is the
First Man"; and so they made man. They made Eve likewise, giving her of
their desire to deceive Adam; and through these things the fashioning of
the world came about by the creation of the prince.

(He says) that God has no part with the world and does not rejoice over it,
because from the beginning he was robbed by the princes and trouble arose
for him. For this reason he sends and steals from them his soul every day
through these lights, that is, the sun and the moon, by which the whole
world and all creation are carried off. The one who spoke with Moses and
the Jews and the priests he says is the prince of darkness; and so the
Christians, the Jews and the pagans are one and the same, worshipping the
same god; for he deceives them in his desires, since he is not the god of
truth. Therefore all who hope in that god who spoke with Moses and the
prophets must be handed over to chains with him, because they did not hope
in the God of truth; for that one spoke with them according to his own
desires.

*(Chapter 13.)* After all this, at the last, he says, as the Elder himself
wrote: when he has made his image manifest, then the Omophoros himself lets
the earth go from him, and so that great fire is let loose which consumes
the whole world; then again they let down the mass (Greek *bōlos*), which
is thrown into the midst of the new age, so that all the souls of the
sinners may be bound for ever. These things will happen when the Statue
comes.

All the emanations are: Jesus in the small ship, and the Mother of Life,
and the twelve helmsmen, and the Maiden of Light, and the third Elder.
Hence the Living Spirit, too, is set in the larger ship, and the wall of
that great fire, and the wall of wind and of air and of water and of the
inner living fire, all of which dwell in the moon (the small light), until
the fire consumes the whole world; in how many years, I have not learned.
And after this there will be the restoration of the two natures: the
princes will dwell in their lower parts, and the Father in the higher,
receiving back what is his own.

This is all the teaching that he handed on to his three disciples, and he
told them to set out for the three regions of the world. Of these, Adda was
allotted the parts of the East, Thomas received the lands of the Syrians,
and Hermas set out for Egypt; and to this day they live there, for the sake
of preaching this doctrine.

input.content:
### Turbo's account, continued (chapters 10–13)

*(Chapter 10 begins:) "I will tell you this too, how the soul is poured over
into five bodies."*

First a little of it is purified in this one; then it is poured over into
a dog, or a camel, or the body of another animal. If it has committed
murder, the soul is poured over into the bodies of lepers; if it has cut the
harvest, into the dumb. The names of the soul are these: mind, sense,
prudence, understanding, thought.

The reapers who reap the harvest are likened to the princes who, sprung
from matter, have been in the darkness since they ate of the armour of the
First Man; that is why they must be poured over into hay, or beans, or
barley, or ears of corn, or vegetables, so that they too may be cut and
mown. And whoever eats bread must himself be eaten, having become bread.
Whoever kills a chicken will himself be a chicken; whoever kills a mouse
will himself be a mouse. If anyone is rich in this world, when he leaves
his body he must be thrown into the body of a poor man, so that he walks
about and begs, and after that he goes to eternal punishment. Since this
body belongs to the princes and to matter, whoever plants a persea tree
must pass through many bodies, until that persea he planted falls. Whoever
builds himself a house will be scattered through all bodies. If anyone
washes himself in water, he wounds his soul; and whoever does not give food
to his (Mani's) Elect will be subjected to the punishments of hell and be
changed into the bodies of hearers, until he does many works of mercy. For
this reason, whatever is best among foods they offer to those Elect.

And when they want to eat bread, they first pray, saying this to the bread:
"I did not reap you, nor grind you, nor knead you, nor put you in the oven;
another made you and brought you to me; I eat you without guilt." And when
he has said this to himself, he answers the one who brought it: "I have
prayed for you"; and so that one goes away. For, as I told you a little
before, if anyone reaps, he will be reaped; so too, if anyone puts corn into
the mill, he will himself be put into the mill; or if he kneads, he will be
kneaded; or if he bakes bread, he will be baked; and for this reason it is
forbidden among them to do work.

And again they say that there are other worlds besides this one we see, on
which the lights of this world rise when they set here. And they say that
if anyone walks on the earth, he hurts the earth; and whoever moves his hand
hurts the air, because the air is the soul of men and animals and birds and
fishes and creeping things and whatever is in this world. For I told you
that this body is not of God, but is of matter and of darkness, and so it
must be darkened.

*(Chapter 11.)* The so-called Paradise is the world. The trees in it are
the desires and the other seductions that corrupt men's thoughts. But that
tree in Paradise from which the good is known is Jesus himself, and his
knowledge, which is in the world; whoever receives it distinguishes good
from evil. The world itself is not God's either, but was formed out of a
part of matter, and so all things are destroyed. What the princes stole
from the First Man is what fills the moon, what is purified every day from
the world. And if a soul goes out that has not known the truth, it is
handed over to the demons, to be tamed in the hell of fire; and after it has
been chastised, it is poured over into other bodies, to be tamed, and so it
is thrown into that great fire until the end.

Of the prophets who are among you he says this: that they are spirits of
the impiety, or lawlessness, of that darkness which rose up in the
beginning; deceived by it, they did not speak in truth; for that prince
blinded their mind. And if anyone follows their words, he will die for
ever, bound in the mass, because he has not learned the knowledge of the
Paraclete.

He commanded his Elect alone, who are no more than seven in number, that
when they have finished eating they should pray, and put on their heads oil
over which spells have been spoken, calling on many names, to strengthen
this faith; but he did not reveal the names to me, for only those seven use
these names. And again, the name Sabaoth, which is great and honoured among
you, he says is the nature of man and the father of desire; and that is
why, he says, the simpler people worship desire, thinking it a god.

*(Chapter 12.)* Of how Adam was made, he says this: that the one who said,
"Come, let us make man in our image and likeness", and after the form we
have seen, is the prince, who says this to the princes his colleagues:
"Come, give me of the light we have received, and let us make (man) after
our form, we who are princes, and after the form we have seen, which is the
First Man"; and so they made man. They made Eve likewise, giving her of
their desire to deceive Adam; and through these things the fashioning of
the world came about by the creation of the prince.

(He says) that God has no part with the world and does not rejoice over it,
because from the beginning he was robbed by the princes and trouble arose
for him. For this reason he sends and steals from them his soul every day
through these lights, that is, the sun and the moon, by which the whole
world and all creation are carried off. The one who spoke with Moses and
the Jews and the priests he says is the prince of darkness; and so the
Christians, the Jews and the pagans are one and the same, worshipping the
same god; for he deceives them in his desires, since he is not the god of
truth. Therefore all who hope in that god who spoke with Moses and the
prophets must be handed over to chains with him, because they did not hope
in the God of truth; for that one spoke with them according to his own
desires.

*(Chapter 13.)* After all this, at the last, he says, as the Elder himself
wrote: when he has made his image manifest, then the Omophoros himself lets
the earth go from him, and so that great fire is let loose which consumes
the whole world; then again they let down the mass (Greek *bōlos*), which
is thrown into the midst of the new age, so that all the souls of the
sinners may be bound for ever. These things will happen when the Statue
comes.

All the emanations are: Jesus in the small ship, and the Mother of Life,
and the twelve helmsmen, and the Maiden of Light, and the third Elder.
Hence the Living Spirit, too, is set in the larger ship, and the wall of
that great fire, and the wall of wind and of air and of water and of the
inner living fire, all of which dwell in the moon (the small light), until
the fire consumes the whole world; in how many years, I have not learned.
And after this there will be the restoration of the two natures: the
princes will dwell in their lower parts, and the Father in the higher,
receiving back what is his own.

This is all the teaching that he handed on to his three disciples, and he
told them to set out for the three regions of the world. Of these, Adda was
allotted the parts of the East, Thomas received the lands of the Syrians,
and Hermas set out for Egypt; and to this day they live there, for the sake
of preaching this doctrine.

     "- **\"No more than seven in number\"** (chapter 11): the Greek of\n  Epiphanius has the same number. It may be a misunderstanding of a rank\n  of the Elect; elsewhere the Elect are many.\n- **The bread prayer** (chapter 10) is the Elect's apology to the food\n  they eat, known also from Augustine and the Coptic *Kephalaia*.\n- **\"The Statue\"** (chapter 13, Latin *statua*, Greek *andrias*) is the\n  Last Statue, the final gathering of the light that rises at the end.\n- **The three disciples** Adda, Thomas and Hermas: Adda (Addai) is the\n  disciple of the Chinese [Traité](traite.html); Thomas is the Thomas of\n  the Coptic *Psalms of Thomas*.\n"),
]
for x, y in R:
    assert x in t, x[:50]
    t = t.replace(x, y, 1)
open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(t)

p = 'research/SCOPE.md'
s = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
a = "(`acta-archelai`, chapters 5 and 7–9, new translation from Beeson's Latin 1906, archive.org `actaarchelaihrsg00hegeuoft`); chapters 10–13 still to do."
assert a in s
s = s.replace(a, "(`acta-archelai`, chapters 5 and 7–13, new translation from Beeson's Latin 1906, archive.org `actaarchelaihrsg00hegeuoft`).")
open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)

p = 'queue.md'
s = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
i = s.index("1. **[Translation] Acta Archelai, Turbo's report chapters 10–13**")
s = s[:i].rstrip('\n') + '\n'
open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)

p = 'devlog.md'
s = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read().rstrip('\n')
s += "\n- 2026-10-21 `acta-archelai`: added Turbo's chapters 10–13 (transmigration, the bread prayer and the ban on work, the other worlds, Paradise and the tree of knowledge as Jesus, the prophets, Adam and Eve, the end and the Statue, the three disciples), translated from Beeson's Latin.\n"
open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
print('ok')

content.text:
I spent the window on translation only, as you asked. Everything is committed and pushed, the site builds, and the texts index went from 6 pages this morning to 36.

**Translated today** (CC BY drafts):
- **From the Chinese:** I finished checking the Traité against the French edition, translated the whole surviving Compendium, and translated the whole Hymnscroll.
- **Turfan texts:** the Šābuhragān, the opening of Mani's Gospel, the Epistle extracts, the cosmogony, the M 4 hymnbook, the Mahrnāmag, and every Old Turkish text in Le Coq's three volumes of *Türkische Manichaica* (1911–1922). That includes an Old Turkish version of the Sermon of the Light-Nous and hymns to Mani.
- **What outsiders quoted from Mani:** al-Nadīm (Mani's life, his teaching, his books, the 76 letters, the commandments and prayers), Theodore bar Konai, Severus of Antioch (the Tree of Life and the Tree of Death), Evodius, and the Acta Archelai (the letter to Marcellus and Turbo's report).

**What you should know:**
- Only the Chinese texts and the Latin (Evodius, Acta Archelai) are translated from the original language. The Turkish, Persian, Parthian, Arabic and Syriac texts are translated from public-domain German or French editions of 1862–1922, and every page says so.
- All of it is draft. Nothing has been checked against a modern edition.
- I first wrote that the Paris half of the Compendium was missing. It wasn't: Taishō already includes it, and I've fixed that note.
- **Left out:** two Christian leaves that turned up among the Turkish texts, and al-Nadīm's list of Muslims accused of Manichaeism. If you want either one included, tell me.
- **Blocked:** the Coptic Psalm Book and Kephalaia, because every scan on archive.org is lending-only.

**Waiting on you:** which public-domain New Testament translation to use; how to rerun the Shangwan substitute images; and, now that the DNS pause is over, the `manichaeism` CNAME record on order.life.

The window closes at 15:00. After that the half-hourly loop keeps going on work that isn't translation.
